anchor: The controller is deliberately minimal, so any advantage traces to the information source, not control sophistication.
claim_text: The controller design is minimal to ensure any advantage comes from the forecast information source rather than control sophistication.

anchor: For the encoder pool, the archived stitched forecast of the image-rate signal (15-second bins, rolling origin) is read at quantile q, converted to a worker count C(t) = ceil(y_hat_q(t) / rho) at per-worker capacity rating rho img/s, and actuated with cold-start lead L and 3-minute scale-down hysteresis.
claim_text: Encoder pool controller uses 15-second bin forecasts at quantile q, converts to worker count via C(t) = ceil(forecast_q / rho) with capacity rating rho img/s, actuated with cold-start lead L and 3-minute scale-down hysteresis.

anchor: The raw head-to-head therefore bundles anticipation with headroom, and the two dials are separated by the p50-forecast, lead-invariance, and reactive-with-headroom ablations below.
claim_text: The forecast vs reactive comparison bundles anticipation and headroom; these are separated via p50-forecast, lead-invariance, and reactive-with-headroom ablations.

anchor: For the language pool, the forecast path replaces the planner's built-in predictor inside Dynamo's SLA-planner loop, so predictive and reactive language-pool policies share the production actuation path end to end; replica lead is enforced by the simulator's native worker-startup delay.
claim_text: Language pool forecast replaces Dynamo planner's built-in predictor; both policies share production actuation path; replica lead enforced by simulator's worker-startup delay.

anchor: The trace's first 1.4 days are consumed as forecast context --- the zero-shot models' rolling history before their first usable 15-second forecast --- and never graded; the remaining 5.60 days form the evaluation span.
claim_text: Trace split: first 1.4 days used as forecast context (not graded), remaining 5.60 days form evaluation span.

anchor: Each [policy constant] is either derived from capacity measurement (the encoder cost model, the belief-to-knee conversion) or swept with all values reported; the headline rating rho=15 is chosen ex post as the conservative operating point.
claim_text: Policy constants derived from capacity measurements or swept; headline rho=15 chosen ex post as conservative operating point.

anchor: The four burst windows pinned at the 588 ms service floor; the calm day 548-734 ms.
claim_text: Burst windows achieve 588 ms p99 encoder delay (service floor); calm day achieves 548-734 ms.

anchor: By contrast, the identically informed reactive controller loses burst3 at every lead and burst4/5 beyond 45 seconds.
claim_text: Reactive controller fails burst3 at all leads and burst4/5 beyond 45s lead.

anchor: On the burst windows the p90 schedule's p99 encoder delay is pinned at 588 ms, the platform's zero-queueing service floor: a full-batch forward (f(64) = 316.4 ms) plus the p99 handoff transfer (272 ms).
claim_text: p90 schedule p99 encoder delay = 588 ms = 316.4 ms (full-batch forward) + 272 ms (p99 handoff transfer).

anchor: The p50 policy is not viable: at rho=15 it clears only 23-24 of its 60 issue-time cells and fails even the calm day (p99 1073 ms at every lead and model).
claim_text: p50 policy at rho=15 passes only 23-24 of 60 cells; fails calm day with p99 1073 ms at all leads/models.

anchor: The calibrated p90 band edge (Chapter 3: empirical coverage 0.88-0.90 at this cadence) converts a point forecast into provisionable headroom.
claim_text: Calibrated p90 band has empirical coverage 0.88-0.90 at 15-second cadence.

anchor: Actuated on true forecast issue time, the p90 policy holds its per-window p99 unchanged across leads from L=15 to 165 s --- the archive's maximum issued lead --- at the 588 ms service floor on every burst window and feasible (below 734 ms) on the calm day.
claim_text: p90 policy p99 lead-invariant from L=15 to 165s at 588 ms (bursts) and <734 ms (calm).

anchor: The reactive twin degrades monotonically with lead toward its never-scaled limit (burst3: 9,481 to 54,170 ms).
claim_text: Reactive controller p99 on burst3 degrades from 9,481 ms to 54,170 ms as lead increases.

anchor: All three foundation models pass all 60 p90/rho=15 cells, consistent with the small cross-model spreads of Chapter 3.
claim_text: All three foundation models (Chronos, Toto, TimesFM) pass all 60 p90/rho=15 factorial cells.

anchor: Swapping Dynamo's own load predictor among ARIMA, Kalman, and Prophet leaves the SLA verdict unchanged (all failing together on the fast onset, burst3).
claim_text: Dynamo's built-in predictors (ARIMA, Kalman, Prophet) all fail burst3 identically.

anchor: The reactive policy, by contrast, is insensitive to rho (13-14 of 20 cells at every rating).
claim_text: Reactive policy passes only 13-14 of 20 cells regardless of rho value.

anchor: Read as a burst detector at true forecast issue time, the p90 band crosses ahead of the observed rate on the gradual onset (burst4, a 345 s usable issue-lead) but lags the fastest onset (burst3, issued at h=1, no usable lead).
claim_text: p90 band leads observed rate on burst4 (345s lead) but lags on burst3 (h=1, no usable lead).

anchor: The closed-loop pass on burst3 therefore does not rest on pre-signal detection: it rests on the calibrated band's graduated headroom, which already sits elevated during the ambient activity before the spike, lifting provisioned capacity to approx 21 workers.
claim_text: Burst3 pass due to graduated headroom elevating capacity to ~21 workers before spike, not pre-signal detection.

anchor: Point and p50 paths, sizing to the mean, detect the same onsets late or never and fail as provisioning signals; the p90 band shows zero false alarms across the calm day for every model.
claim_text: p50/point forecasts fail as provisioning signals; p90 band has zero false alarms on calm day for all models.

anchor: Running the reactive controller with the tail-aware headroom it was denied --- the trailing-window p90 of the observed image rate at the same rho=15 and lead, but still no forecast --- passes the slow onset (burst1) and week scale but fails the one-minute onset (burst3, p99 1,973-11,568 ms against the forecast's 588 ms).
claim_text: Reactive with trailing-window p90 headroom passes burst1 but fails burst3 (p99 1,973-11,568 ms vs forecast's 588 ms).

anchor: Driving the identical encoder loop with a forward EWMA point path --- its p90 calibrated on the 1.4-day context to the same 0.88-0.90 coverage by three standard schemes --- exposes a coverage-versus-cost bind.
claim_text: Forward EWMA with p90 calibrated to 0.88-0.90 coverage on 1.4-day context shows coverage-cost tradeoff.

anchor: The two cheap calibrations clear the burst-masked week aggregate but fail the fast and high-volume onsets under per-episode grading, and the one calibration that clears every episode over-provisions at 1.09x static.
claim_text: Two EWMA calibrations pass aggregate but fail per-episode; one passes all episodes but costs 1.09x static.

anchor: Only the zero-shot foundation-model band clears every episode and beats static (0.62x).
claim_text: Zero-shot foundation model band passes all episodes at 0.62x static cost.

claim_text: Chronos control reproduces results within <1% run noise.

anchor: The planner sizes replicas as ceil(d_hat / r_hat) where r_hat is its belief about per-replica throughput (measured in-loop: median 10.07 req/s per TP2 replica); the SLA-relevant capacity is instead the measured tail knee r_tail, the largest offered rate a replica sustains under the tail SLA (1.62 req/s on burst1's mix; [1.26, 1.44] on burst4, the binding mix).
claim_text: Planner uses r_hat=10.07 req/s (median); tail knee r_tail=1.62 req/s (burst1) and 1.26-1.44 req/s (burst4).

anchor: Scaling the forecast by r_hat/r_tail makes the mean-based planner land on tail-adequate replica counts, and validation flips exactly at the formula's boundary on both windows tested.
claim_text: Scaling forecast by r_hat/r_tail achieves tail-adequate replica counts; validation flips at formula boundary.

anchor: A ~14% margin above the binding knee is retained as policy, since r_tail is mix-dependent and replays show ~4% p99 noise.
claim_text: Policy retains ~14% margin above binding knee due to mix-dependence and ~4% p99 noise.

anchor: On burst windows the resulting language fleet costs about what the burst-sized static optimum does; the language-side saving is cross-window (TP1x2 on calm traffic, half the burst fleet's GPUs).

anchor: The replay is open-loop: arrivals follow the trace regardless of experienced latency, so overload cannot shed or defer demand as clients would.
claim_text: Replay is open-loop: arrivals follow trace regardless of latency; no client shedding/backpressure modeled.

anchor: The inter-pool handoff is priced single-stream (~1.6 MB per image); Qwen3-VL's DeepStack projections quadruple that payload, and a sensitivity replay of the aggregate at the 4x payload on the modeled 25 Gbps link raises p99 handoff from 272 to 1,087 ms (encoder-delay p99 1,404 ms --- an SLA violation from transfer alone).
claim_text: Handoff: single-stream ~1.6MB/image; 4x payload on 25Gbps raises p99 handoff 272->1,087ms, encoder p99 1,404ms (SLA violation).

anchor: At the 4x payload every policy violates the bound, including the deployable static fleet, because the 1,087 ms handoff floor is common to all.
claim_text: At 4x payload, all policies violate SLA (1,087ms handoff floor common to all).

anchor: The 588 ms floor therefore assumes an embedding-only handoff or a >=100 Gbps inter-pool fabric, which restores the quoted numbers for every policy exactly.
claim_text: 588ms floor assumes embedding-only handoff or >=100Gbps fabric.

anchor: Per-pool leads are swept as constants, not stochastic.
claim_text: Per-pool leads swept as constants, not stochastic.

anchor: The two out-of-span episodes (burst2/6) are graded only by the forecast-free baselines of Chapter 4, never by a forecast policy.
claim_text: Burst2/6 graded only by forecast-free baselines (Ch4), never by forecast policy.

anchor: Replay-level p99 noise is ~4%; no quoted policy contrast is within that band.
claim_text: Replay p99 noise ~4%; no policy contrast within that band.

anchor: vLLM's own Qwen3-VL vision tower matches AIC to within 12.8% across the whole N<=64 serving regime, because AIC's collected operators are vLLM's kernels.
claim_text: vLLM Qwen3-VL vision tower matches AIC within 12.8% for N<=64.

anchor: Replaying the winning p90/rho=15 schedule with the encoder repriced at the directly-measured vLLM f(N) leaves the schedule's provisioned worker-time --- the cost-ratio numerator --- unchanged and the static C=8 denominator feasible, so the reported 0.62x holds on measured standalone vLLM cost, not only the AIC model.
claim_text: 0.62x holds on measured vLLM cost (not just AIC model); static C=8 feasible.

anchor: Splitting the expanding-context span (999,599 requests over 6.998 days, longer than the 5.60-day span the headline is priced on, and reproducing its aggregate ratio at 0.612x) into seven disjoint 24-hour folds leaves the headline quantities not fold-invariant.
claim_text: Expanding-context span: 999,599 requests, 6.998 days, aggregate ratio 0.612x; 7 folds not fold-invariant.

anchor: The encoder cost ratio against the deployed C=8 fleet ranges 0.47-1.10x over the five burst-bearing folds, rho=15 is feasible in six of seven folds but cheapest in none.
claim_text: Encoder cost ratio across folds: 0.47-1.10x; rho=15 feasible in 6/7 folds, cheapest in 0.

anchor: The policy misses the bound on the fold containing the e13 onset (encoder-delay p99 1,262 ms), where a static C=5 fleet passes for only 3% more worker-time.
claim_text: Policy fails on e13 onset fold (p99=1,262ms); static C=5 passes for 3% more worker-time.

anchor: The language pool's fold ratios run 0.93-3.81x against the same-fold static comparator --- above parity in six of seven folds, since short folds amortize nothing.
claim_text: Language pool fold ratios: 0.93-3.81x vs static; above parity in 6/7 folds.

anchor: The fixed C=8 encoder denominator is an accounting reference, not per-fold re-optimized (one truncated fold's C=8 row ends with a non-empty queue and is marked infeasible).
claim_text: C=8 encoder denominator is accounting reference, not per-fold re-optimized; one fold C=8 infeasible.

anchor: The ratio is monotone in each fold's offered image load (a 12x demand spread produces part of the range by construction).
claim_text: Cost ratio monotone in fold image load (12x demand spread).

anchor: The folds are disjoint test windows but not training-independent, each forecast conditioned on its predecessors.
claim_text: Folds are disjoint test windows but not training-independent (forecasts conditioned on predecessors).

anchor: They share one trace's tenant mix, size distribution and hardware calibration, differing only in time --- evidence about temporal variability within one trace and nothing else.
claim_text: Folds share tenant mix, size distribution, hardware calibration; only time differs.

anchor: The rho frontier's cheapest feasible setting sits at a grid endpoint in seven of eight windows swept, so no interior optimum is licensed.
claim_text: rho frontier cheapest feasible at grid endpoint in 7/8 windows; no interior optimum.

anchor: Generalization to other workloads, models, and datacenters remains unaddressed.
claim_text: Generalization to other workloads/models/datacenters unaddressed.

anchor: On the encoder pool, forecasting the pool's own signal at the calibrated p90 edge holds the tail SLA at every forecast-issued lead, including the one-minute onset that defeats an identically informed reactive controller at every lead.
claim_text: Encoder pool: p90 forecast holds SLA at all leads including 1-min onset; reactive fails at all leads.

anchor: On the language pool the same forecast passes bursts under realistic replica leads only through the tail-aware capacity conversion --- a measured belief-to-knee ratio, tested under a held forecast cursor rather than a second anticipation test --- which repairs the mean-based sizing defect shared by every reactive configuration tested.
claim_text: Language pool: forecast passes bursts via tail-aware conversion (belief-to-knee ratio) under held cursor; fixes mean-sizing defect.

anchor: Priced over the covered week, the policy meets the SLA in aggregate and per-episode at 0.62 times the deployable static encoder fleet's worker-time --- a week-scale figure (per burst window, every arm costs more than static).
claim_text: Week-scale: policy meets SLA aggregate and per-episode at 0.62x static encoder worker-time; per burst window all arms cost more than static.
